- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 10–20%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model underestimates; increase forecast lows by 10–20%.
- After a sharp spike in forecast (e.g., >50% above recent mean), model often overshoots; cap next period’s forecast at 1.5x prior peak.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to mean-revert; apply smoothing to forecast mean over 3–5 periods.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts volatility in high-sentiment periods; reduce forecast variance by 20–30% when sentiment > 0.67.
- If forecast is > 2.5x recent average and sentiment is neutral or negative, model is likely overconfident; apply downward bias of 15–25%.
- When sentiment is flat (0.00 or 0.33) for 3+ days, model drifts toward historical mean; adjust forecast to align with 14-day rolling average.
